Meeting header:

Auto-summary:
Windfall ran the week-3 bench against their incumbent (CurrentVendor AIServ). Redwood showed head-to-head numbers with lower median and 95th latency for the short chat path but slightly higher 99th under heavy burst. Throughput (tokens/sec) looked favorable with Redwood's batching + prefix cache when QPS steady. Customer asked about VPC private deploy latency, KMS encryption overhead, and fallback to smaller model to preserve tail SLOs. Actionables: share detailed per-route percentiles, routing playbook, and schedule in-lab head-to-head.

Topics:
- Week 3 benchmark: median/95/99 latency vs incumbent
- Throughput and unit cost per token estimate
- Routing decision: primary->redwood, fallback->incumbent or smaller quantized variant
- Security/Private deployment constraints (V P C, KMS, audit logs)
- Next steps and in-lab head-to-head run scheduling

Transcript body:
[00:00] Samir (Redwood): hey everyone, thanks for jumping on. can we do quick roll call?
[00:08] Dana (Windfall): Dana here, ravi and marta with me as well.
[00:12] Ravi (Windfall): morning, yeah we got the week 3 runs in, excited to walk through.
[00:16] Samir: great. Elena will run through the numbers and tao will cover routing playbook.
[00:24] Elena (Redwood): ok, so quick context — we re-ran the same workload you sent last week, matching prompt distribution and 95th token lengths. baseline is CurrentVendor AIServ v3.1, we ran 10k requests over two sessions to capture warm and cold tails.
[00:40] Elena: median latency on the chat path was 54 ms on redwood vs 78 ms baseline, 95th was 210 ms vs 310 ms. 99th we saw 780 ms vs 640 ms — so tail is higher for us in that particular burst window, likely queueing under continuous batching.
[01:05] Dana: ok that's interesting — median better, 99th worse, that 99th discrepancy is concerning for us because our SLO is 800 ms 99th.
[01:12] Elena: totally, yep we noticed that and dug into the KV cache behavior — the cold prefixes and a couple of long-request spikes caused a backlog. our fix options: 1) aggressive per-model slot reservation (dedicated), 2) fallback routing to a smaller quantized variant for long tails, or 3) change batching window to prefer latency (lower batch size at cost per-token).
[01:33] Ravi: what's the quantized variant trade? does output quality drop a lot?
[01:36] Elena: slight truncation on nuanced completions, we recommend running a small eval set — we can attach eval diffs. for many instruction prompts the difference is minimal.
[01:46] Marta: are we able to do VPC private deployment for the dedicated slot? security wants the control plane in our V P C and keys in our K M S.
[01:53] Samir: yes, we support private deployments. control plane can be customer-managed. KMS integration is supported, full audit logs. we'll share SOC2 + architecture diagram after.
[02:03] Dana: overhead? any latency hit when KMS rotates or we use H S M?
[02:08] Tao (Redwood): small on initial handshake for key unwrap, negligible per-request if we cache the data key locally. typical numbers are 2-5 ms once keys are cached; cold rotation adds a spike but not per-token.
[02:22] Dana: ok that sounds fine.
[02:25] Elena: on throughput, redwood showed 1.8x tokens/sec under steady QPS vs baseline for the large model, mainly due to continuous batching and our prefix cache. unit cost estimate after quantization and batching suggestions drops ~30% vs baseline for your workload.
[02:44] Ravi: can you share the config we used for the run — batch size, sequence length assumptions, warmup steps?
[02:49] Elena: yes, we'll attach the runner config and the CSV. note we intentionally left burst policy permissive which inflated 99th.
[02:56] Dana: can you explain the burst policy? our traffic is spiky, like 200 to 1200 RPS for minutes.
[03:03] Tao: burst policy determines how much we accept above reserved capacity before routing fallback. if you set strict reserved capacity with small burst, you'll avoid queueing but see throttling; if you allow larger bursts, we handle via short queues and batching which improves median but can hurt tail.
[03:18] Ravi: could we run a variant that pins dedicated slots for peak windows and uses hosted for base?
[03:23] Samir: yes — hybrid: reserved slots for base SLO, autoscale for peaks + graceful fallback to quantized variant for tails. that's what the routing playbook proposes.
[03:32] Marta: what's the fallback latency delta if routed to quantized variant?
[03:36] Elena: median goes down to ~40 ms, 95th to 160 ms, 99th ~420 ms, and quality drop is minor on short instructions.
[03:47] Dana: how about fallback to incumbent instead of quantized variant?
[03:50] Elena: we can fallback to any compatible model including your incumbent merchant; downside is egress/handshake overhead and possible auth/token rotation to another vendor. also, you'd pay two vendors during failover windows.
[04:05] Ravi: cost question — you said unit cost down 30% with quantize + batching. what's absolute cost per 1M tokens?
[04:11] Samir: rough sketch: baseline vendor is ~ $1,400 per 1M tokens in your run; with redwood optimized profile we estimate ~$980 per 1M after batching & quantization. dedicated contracts change the math — we can run committed slot numbers.
[04:28] Dana: please send an example committed slot math.
[04:31] Samir: will do.
[04:33] Elena: one more datapoint — while median improved, we saw sensitivity to request size variance. when token length spikes above 1.8x median, batching groups fewer requests and queueing increases. causes a tail.
[04:47] Ravi: could we change client to send truncated prefix or use token budget?
[04:51] Elena: yes, truncating non-critical context helps, or you can leverage our prefix/K V cache so repeated context doesn't count towards seq length after warm cache.
[05:02] Marta: ok. security wise, can we get the full audit logs and an ingestion timeline?
[05:07] Tao: yes audit logs available, can forward retention SLAs. note for private deployment we can store logs in your S3 with export TTL you control.
[05:16] Dana: great. on scheduling in-lab head-to-head, next tuesday is good for us — we want to run the same 10k run with both vendors side-by-side and compare traces.
[05:26] Samir: we'll set up lab runner, can you confirm the exact request pattern and sample keys?
[05:30] Ravi: I'll drop the pattern and the p95 token length; also will share staging V P C peering creds via your secure link.
[05:36] Elena: we'll prepare a lean runner config: 3 runs — baseline, redwood default, redwood latency-tuned. collect per-route percentiles, token-level traces, and kernel selection logs.
[05:48] Dana: do you capture kernel selection? sometimes your runtime picks a fallback kernel and we see perf oddities.
[05:54] Tao: yes we capture kernel path and quantization flags in the trace export. we'll redact kernel internals but surface timing and model variant used.
[06:05] Marta: what about SLA? if we go dedicated, do you provide SLO credits for missed 99th?
[06:10] Samir: yes dedicated customers can receive credits per contract; we'll cover contract language in the enterprise packet.
[06:17] Dana: ok let's recap next steps.
